agents.name: Claude Code

surface_source.quote: Tools + playbook for babysitting a Claude/Fable CLI session running in a tmux

agents.quote:
The project is run by three long-lived Claude sessions. The human (the parent)
gives high-level direction, usually by texting one agent over Remote Control.

also.quote: I have one window per work tree, each a single tab that is just a regular shell, and then as many tabs as I think I need for concurrent Claude Code instances on that worktree.

history.value: Claude Desktop + codemcp (his own MCP server)
history.quote: Make Claude Desktop a pair programming assistant by installing codemcp.

NOTICE: claude code is available with Anthropic's $20/mo subscription, so I consider
codemcp fully obsolete.

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: Codex shell commands may not have working external internet access, even when the local machine does.

history.quote: ScubaDuck was implemented with OpenAI Codex in the cloud (not the CLI tool).
Claude Opus is not fast enough for single session interactive.

review_style.value: Reads every line, steers with questions and edits
review_style.quote: This is NOT a workflow for letting the AI autonomously write tons of code. You’re going to be reading every single line it produces.

also.quote: If you treat AI generated output as code to read, you have already lost the game.

harness.value: iTerm2 + tmux -CC to a remote GPU box, three worktrees, Sapling
harness.quote: Because I am typically doing work on a GPU system, these sessions are remote, so I use iTerm2 + tmux -CC (tmux control mode) to conveniently have multiple windows and tabs in native UI.

parallelism.quote: The basic development flow here is I have three work streams going in parallel:

history.quote: I’d sometimes have as many as five instances going

rules_files.value: Per-repo CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md; piano-pad's assigns roles to three agents
rules_files.quote: **Your role is the one whose directory you are running in.** Read your charter

hooks.quote:
#       UserPromptSubmit -> chunk-reminder.sh   (prevention: small-turns context)
#       StopFailure      -> stopfailure-unwedge.sh (recovery: self re-prompt)

signature.caption: restack parallel agents
signature.why: Our pick: two Sapling aliases let agents in several worktrees amend one shared stack without trampling each other.
signature.quote: I find these two commands cover the majority of situations that show up when you are working with parallel agents!

archetype.why: Reads every line the agent writes and runs no orchestrator, just tabs per worktree.

signature_quote.value: If you treat AI generated output as code to read, you have already lost the game.
